D. FLORA AND FAUNA
Alma CNRA:
In the Alma area vegetation consists of residential and street landscaping, as well as the bark landscaping in the Alma Tot Lot. Street trees are sparse along some sections like Little Orchard Street. In contrast to this, mature Sycamores and Elms line Ford Avenue and other large trees are found randomly throughout the area. For example, located to the east of Pomona Avenue near Roberts Court. there are two large Coast Redwoods, an enormous Acacia and Box Elder trees, while near Bellevue Avenue, there are two old Canary Island Date Palms. Additionally, mature Carob and Olive trees grow along Alma Avenue and Ford Avenue respectively. The most common street trees in the area are Walnut, Elm and Sycamore. The animal life in Alma is similar to that found in the Campus and developed sections of Mayfair and Olinder.
Alviso CNRA:
The Alviso area encompasses a wide diversity of vegetation and wildlife, ranging from the salt marsh and estuary habit to residential landscaping. The residential landscaping is a typical of most urban residential areas in San Jose because there are no curbs, gutters and sidewalks and thus yards and lawns are poorly defined and often mostly barren. However, there are several mature trees, shrubs and lawns to be found, such as at the stately old house on Elizabeth Street next to the railroad tracks. Elsewhere along streets and in front yards some of the most frequently planted trees include Pine, California Pepper, Blue Gum, Deodora Cedar, Elm, Coast Redwood, Date Palm, Poplar and Weeping Willow. In contrast to much of Alviso, there is well manicured landscaping around the Alviso Family Health Center Building. Animal life found in association with the developed parts of Alviso is typical of most residential areas. While there is not a sufficient tree density to support Fox Squirrels, there are House Finches, Western Robins and Starlings to be found.
In the vacant lots and undeveloped areas of Alviso there are annual grasses and "weedy" species, mostly of European origin, some examples of which are Bristly Ox Tongue, Prickly Wild Lettuce and Curly Dock. Along ditches and drainages Cat-Tails and Sweet Fennel are frequent. Across these open grassy area one finds Western Meadowlarks, Beechey Ground Squirrels and the like.
Guadalupe River passes through the Alviso area and is lined with cat-tails, and some Willows. The river, with its brackish water provides a habitat for several species of fish, as well as ducks, and other water and shore birds. In the area surrounding Alviso to the north and west there is saltmarsh with such typical plants as Saltgrass, Pickleweed and Alkali Heath. The saltmarsh community provides a habitat for a wide variety of wildlife. For example, one finds Common and Snowy Egrets, Shoveler, Willet, Killdeer, Short-billed Dowitcher to name just a few. The two most important species here are California Clapper Rail and the Saltmarsh Harvest House (Red-bellied Harvest Mouse) because they are endangered species. In order to preserve these species and their saltmarsh habitat, a National Wildlife Refuge covering several hundred acres has been established to the north of Alviso.
